sections.title: How to use this hub
sections.body:
This is the central working record for ZeroBooze’s brand, website, social, marketing, partnerships, sales, recruitment, and community communications. It starts from the client’s intent, rather than assuming the current site or earlier drafts are the answer.


Evidence labels:
CONFIRMED DIRECTION: an explicit statement by Keith in an email or his September notes.
COLLABORATOR PROPOSAL: a recommendation from Dustin or another contributor, without assuming Keith approved it.
INTERPRETATION: our reading of the pattern across sources.
PROPOSED COPY: new language written for review.
FUTURE / UNVERIFIED: a plan or claim that cannot yet be presented as an available service or established result.


Each strategic point and copy module includes source IDs. The source register at the end identifies the email files and links back to them. Dates cited in the discussion are the original conversation dates, rather than simply the October forwarding dates.


Coverage: the message text and forwarded conversations in 39 individual email files; Keith’s September 2026 DOCX attachment; the Anti Talking Points PDF attachment; the current website’s homepage, founder story, notebook, and store preview; and all four supplied video transcripts. Sections 21–23 add transcript-based social content and Keith’s bio. Design files, photographs, legal agreements, and other embedded attachments have not all been visually reviewed. Transcript wording is source material; actual recordings, clip timecodes, and picture edits still require verification.


Later additions should record source, owner, date, audience, channel, availability status, copy status, and approval. Preserve earlier decisions in the decision log when direction changes.

sections.title: What Keith is trying to build
sections.body:
CONFIRMED DIRECTION
ZeroBooze is bigger than merchandise. Keith wants empathy and support, acknowledgment of the individual in each story, and navigation toward life without alcohol. He describes the ambition as the “Waze” of sobriety. Community and in-residence development should move in parallel, on different timelines. [E32 attachment, Sept. 12]


His priority audiences are the Recovering and the Quietly Concerned. People own their story and their path. Accountability matters, but the tone should carry it subtly and deliberately. His central distinction: ZB cannot do the work FOR someone, but can do it WITH them. [E32]


He wants community participation, shared stories, eventual gatherings, useful resources, and invitations to help shape the brand. Merchandise remains available for those who want it; it is ancillary. [E09, July 7; E32]


He wants the brand to feel premium, conversational, and clear without being in someone’s face. Softness does not come naturally to him; he explicitly asks for help balancing his directness. He wants the founder story early, while preserving the feeling that this is about the visitor. [E32]


INTERPRETATION
Keith is a builder who wants lived experience to lead to useful change. His frustration with familiar recovery conventions fuels ambition, but his strongest public message is practical companionship and personal ownership. “Disruption” should be demonstrated by concrete choices and evidence as they develop.


The brand needs two speeds: a clear, useful community experience people can enter now, and a longer-term vision with transparent milestones. A visitor should not have to decipher which is which. [E20, E25, E29–E30, E32; W01–W03]


WORKING POSITIONING — proposed
ZeroBooze is a community taking shape around life without alcohol, built from lived experience and grounded in the belief that you own your story and your path. It brings people, perspectives, and useful resources together, while working toward a broader future in recovery and support. [E09, E23, E32]


SHORT DESCRIPTION — proposed
Life without alcohol. Your story. Your path. A community to walk with you.


Use that as descriptive copy, not an assumed approved tagline. Keith agreed that the name can stand alone. [E25, Aug. 28]

sections.title: Audience priorities
sections.body:
The Recovering — primary
Keith defines this audience as day one through five years in his internal notes. Their need: continued support, useful next steps, and a connection beyond a single episode of care. Message: you are doing the work; you do not have to navigate every part alone. Avoid making the five-year boundary a public clinical definition. [E32]


The Quietly Concerned — primary
People at the doorstep of change who have not taken that step. Their need: recognition, privacy, and a manageable invitation. Message: you can start with a question. Do not assume they identify with recovery or publicly disclose concerns. [E25, E23, E32]


The Recovered — secondary
Keith’s internal definition is five-plus years. Their need: identity, connection, contribution, and respect for experience. Message: your perspective can help someone find their next step. Avoid suggesting they have crossed a universal finish line. [E32]


The Sober Curious — secondary
People considering alcohol-free living, including for health or lifestyle reasons, without assuming an abuse history. Message: there is room for your reason. [E23, E32]


Additional communication audiences — proposed
Loved ones seeking a way to support someone; professionals and referral partners assessing credibility; potential employees and collaborators; partners and donors; investors considering the future residential vision. These require different proof and calls to action. Do not make investor ambition the homepage’s primary message.


Decision history
Dustin’s July 7 recommendation emphasized people already living without alcohol and deferred sober curious outreach. Keith’s September notes broadened the model and explicitly prioritized the Recovering and Quietly Concerned. The September notes guide this draft. [E09 → E25/E23 → E32]

sections.title: Source foundation — earlier voice & message pillars
sections.body:
SOURCE AND DECISION HISTORY
This earlier working interpretation is preserved for reference. The proposed October 26 Brand pillars and Voice & tone modules provide the current organized system for review. No client approval is implied.

VOICE — proposed application of Keith’s direction
Conversational, direct, warm, and sure of itself. Use short clear sentences alongside natural paragraphs. Address a person rather than a demographic category. Make room for uncertainty without sounding vague. Offer participation without demanding disclosure. Use empathy with accountability; do not moralize or promise to save anyone. [E10, E18–E19, E23–E25, E32; W02]


PILLAR A: Your story belongs to you
You own your story and your path. Different histories can share a common connection without being flattened into the founder’s experience. [E23, E32; W03]
Use in: homepage, About, invitations to share, community guidelines.


PILLAR B: We can walk with you
Support and useful navigation accompany personal effort. Make the next step feel approachable and specific. [E32]
Use in: Resources, Contact, support descriptions, after-care communications when a service exists.


PILLAR C: Belonging comes first
Community is a priority, not a by-product of shopping. Merchandise expresses connection; purchasing is not a condition of participation. [E09, E22, E32]
Use in: homepage order, Store, email welcome, social.


PILLAR D: Build deliberately; show the work
The brand is in development. Updates, questions, and milestones can make progress visible and invite collaboration. [E24, E32; W03]
Use in: Horizon, notebook, recruitment, investor materials.


PILLAR E: Question conventions with care
Challenge assumptions about the experience of recovery, with specific reasons and substantiation. Lead with what improves life for the individual. [E02, E25, E29]
Use in: thought leadership and program development; avoid unsupported comparisons in public sales copy.


Recognition, permission, and relief are a useful editorial test proposed by Dustin, not a documented final emotional choice by Keith. Pair that test with Keith’s explicit “empathy and support.” [E19 vs. E32]


BEFORE / AFTER — editorial examples
Generic: “Embark on an inspiring journey.”
Proposed: “Find a next step that makes sense for you.”
Generic: “We will transform your life.”
Proposed: “You own the work. We want to help you find the people and resources to support it.”
Generic: “Our facility treats patients.”
Proposed future description: “Our planned residence will be shaped around the people who come here for recovery.”

sections.title: Keith’s language guide
sections.body:
Source: E39, ZB Anti Talking Points PDF. These are Keith’s preferred contrasts, recorded faithfully. They are an internal direction list, not evidence that planned clinical offerings or outcomes exist.


Avoid → Keith’s preferred wording
Treatment → Relief / Recovery
Journey → Path
One Day at a Time → Your own Horizon
“AA” Foundation → Ownership Foundation
Traditional / Accepted Treatment → Disruption Treatment
Patients → Resident Guests
Alcoholism → Abuse
Inspire → Self-Realization
30 Days & 60 Days → 45 Days & 75 Days
Acceptance → Admission
12% Outcome → 35% Outcome (3X)
Self-Serve Post Care → Administered Post Care
Static / Accepted Modalities → Disruption Modalities
Groups → Community
Insurance Pay → High Self-Pay
Profit Focused → Success Focused
Varying Residential Rules → Regimented Residential Rules


Additional explicit preferences
Facility: avoid in public brand language; Dave’s current brief confirms this preference. Proposed replacement: “Our Residence,” subject to confirming there is a single residential property. “Our Spaces” works if the page covers several locations or nonresidential settings.
Quietly Committed: superseded by Quietly Concerned. [E25, E23, E32]
“Live inside”: Keith questioned it; use experience, commonality, expression, or support instead. [E23]
Road: Keith explicitly asks to replace it with path. [E32]
“Inspire / Journey / Celebrate” as a logo lockup: challenged by Dustin, followed by Keith’s pivot toward the name alone. [E15, E25]
“Celebrating Sobriety, Inspiring Recovery”: considered, then set aside; not the default tagline. [E21, E25]


HOW TO APPLY
Prefer recovery, relief, support, path, ownership, community, and life without alcohol. “Resident Guests” belongs in an actual residential context; use person, community member, or participant elsewhere. Avoid defining someone as “an abuser.” Even though “Abuse” appears on Keith’s list, person-centered plain language often removes the need for a label.


The list is not a mechanical word-replacement tool. “Admission” can mean entering a program; do not replace emotional acceptance everywhere. “Disruption Treatment” still uses a word Keith otherwise dislikes, so retain that exact contrast in the internal register while writing public copy around the specific approach.


Do not convert 45/75-day plans, self-pay positioning, administered post care, residential rules, or numerical outcomes into current service facts. All require operational confirmation. The 12% / 35% / 3X line is an unverified claim and is excluded from public copy.


Respect different approaches to recovery. Ownership is the brand’s organizing idea; it does not establish that the brand rejects all spiritual or peer-support options. The PDF’s appendix describes several alternatives with differing philosophies, including 12-step approaches. Do not copy that appendix as verified current resource guidance without checking the original providers.

LATEST LANGUAGE UPDATE — October 14, 2026
Dave’s direction: Patients is wording to avoid; Resident Guests is the preferred wording. This supersedes the earlier Patient → Resident entry. Use the residential term in the appropriate context.

BRAND NAME — confirmed October 14, 2026
Always write ZeroBooze as one word, with a capital Z and B. See the Brand name & spelling module.

sections.title: Decisions, tensions, and evidence boundaries
sections.body:
DECISIONS TO CARRY FORWARD
Community is a priority. [Keith, E09, July 7]
Let ZeroBooze stand on its own; the tagline discussion has changed. [Keith, E25, Aug. 28; E21 forwarding note]
Use Quietly Concerned and prioritize that audience alongside the Recovering. [Keith, E23/E32, Sept. 4/12]
Keep merchandise secondary. [Keith, E32]
Use conversational copy with deliberate accountability. [Keith, E32]
Develop community and residential ambitions in parallel on different timelines. [Keith, E32]
Use opt-in updates and communications. [Keith, E32]
Allow both Gratitude and Interview in Progress to coexist as personal practices. [Keith, E13, Sept. 19]
Preserve a Horizon space for future ambitions. [Keith, E20, Sept. 7]


TENSIONS TO RESOLVE THROUGH DESIGN AND COPY
Quiet public voice versus “let’s break things” internal energy: keep the public welcome calm; demonstrate challenge through substantive content. [E25/E32]
Founder authenticity versus a community larger than one person: use Keith’s story to open the door, then turn toward the visitor and other voices. [E22/E32]
Lifestyle brand versus residential provider: one brand can connect them, but available services and future plans must be unmistakable. Dustin suggested separate sites; Keith later emphasized parallel efforts. Architecture remains a decision, not a settled mandate. [E30/E32]
Privacy versus direct access: Keith wants a brand-facing conversation channel, not his personal number prominently displayed. Verify workflow and response expectations before activating it. [E32; W01]
Premium versus accessible: dignity and clarity should create the premium feeling without implying everyone must shop or afford residential care.


CLAIMS HELD FROM PUBLIC COPY
Claims about the historical origin of 28-day programs: present in E25/E29, not independently substantiated here.
Numerical recovery outcomes and “3X”: present in E39, no definition, denominator, follow-up period, or supporting evidence supplied.
Market-size, alcohol-cancer awareness, competitor revenue, and closure assertions in E17: research leads, not approved proof points.
Specific advocate identities and willingness to participate: E03 is too ambiguous to establish an endorsement.
Clinical modalities, staffing, licenses, accreditations, program eligibility, pricing, insurance terms, residence location, opening date, and availability: not confirmed for launch.
Shock Pulse Medical: separate venture in E07/E35/E36. Do not imply its technology or services are part of ZeroBooze without an explicit decision and evidence.

sections.title: Current website review
sections.body:
Reviewed October 13, 2026 at https://zerobooze.life/ through the visible site.


W01 — Homepage
Current lead: “You remember the moment.” Describes a brand taking shape around life without alcohol. Includes founder story, community, notebook, hat, and conversation invitation. Retain the human welcome and room for different experiences; make the purpose clearer sooner. The opening assumes a defining moment, which may fit less well for sober curious visitors.


W02 — Founder story, https://zerobooze.life/story
Current title: “I’m still in it.” The story acknowledges alcohol’s effects, prior attempts at change, choosing care, and building ZeroBooze while still in recovery. Keep its candor. Replace dated early-recovery timing and confirm personal details before republication. The personal thank-you names family and supporters; retain only with Keith’s approval of placement and wording. Use “recovery” rather than “treatment” in new brand copy while preserving exact quoted source records.


W03 — Keith’s Notebook, opened from homepage
Topics: common denominator across different histories; development of a first center in Florida; and the need for clinical, design, and construction expertise. It expressly states the center is not open. Preserve that availability distinction. These entries corroborate a development effort, not an operational residence.


Current site limitation
Texting is explicitly a preview and is not connected. Do not publish “Text ZeroBooze” as a working action until verified. Navigation and page structure differ from the requested new sitemap.


This review is a baseline, not a commitment to reuse the current design or all copy. The website draft below rebuilds the message around the primary audiences and Keith’s later direction.


W04 — Store, https://zerobooze.life/merch
The visible collection preview lists hat, cap, visor, tumbler, polo, jug, and clear tumbler. It expressly says products, prices, and options are proposed for review and purchases are not enabled. The repeated $35 display is not adopted as approved pricing. Confirm the catalog, stock, fulfillment, and checkout before publishing Store copy.

sections.title: Recommended website architecture
sections.body:
Recommended main navigation:
About | Our Residence | Services | Resources | Store | Contact
Home is reached through the logo. Add Horizon as a visible secondary link and a prominent homepage module.


Home: explain what ZeroBooze means, invite the priority audiences, introduce community and Keith, and offer a useful next step.
About / Our Story: the belief, founder origin, audience, and approach. Prefer a personal story to a conventional resume bio. [E18, E29–E30, E32]
Our Residence: proposed replacement for Facility. While development continues, this page describes the intention and progress; it must not resemble an admissions page.
Services: show available ways to engage first; label any clinical or residential offerings in development. If no services are operational, consider “Support” for the public navigation, with “Services” retained as the working sitemap label.
Resources: practical guidance, selected links, shared experiences, and the ongoing notebook. Proposed notebook label: “Along the Path.” Keith asked to reconsider “Notebook”; this label is a recommendation, not his approved wording. [E32]
Store: merchandise and expression, with truthful product information and clear fulfillment policies.
Contact: a modest, usable invitation for general inquiries, stories, partners, and recruitment.
Horizon: future centers, resources, virtual support, beverages/nutrition, and a charitable foundation, without implying launch dates. [E20, E39]


Primary conversion recommendation: a conversation or optional updates, supported by useful Resources. Buying is secondary. Keith’s stated goal is helping people live without alcohol and tell others, with traffic and positive feedback as early signals. [E32]


Copy below is PROPOSED COPY. Editorial notes and source notes are not part of the public pages. Bracketed facts are missing inputs, not text to publish.

sections.body:
HERO
Life without alcohol.
A path that’s yours.


ZeroBooze began with someone who needed it first. We’re building a community for people living without alcohol, people finding their way toward it, and people beginning to ask what might change.


Your story is yours. There’s room for it here.


Primary button: Explore Resources
Secondary button: Meet ZeroBooze


Sources / status: proposed from E23/E32, supported by E09/E19. “Community” is an ambition in development; verify the actual participation experience before launch.


COMMUNITY MODULE
You don’t have to have it all figured out.


Maybe you’re in recovery. Maybe something about your drinking has been on your mind. Maybe you’ve chosen life without alcohol for a reason entirely your own.


We want ZeroBooze to be a place to find useful perspectives, make a connection, and take a next step on your terms.


Button: Start a Conversation
Sources: E23/E32. Activate only with a working channel.

Built from a life. Built for more than one.


Keith Polaski started ZeroBooze in the early days of his own sobriety. His experience is where this began. It’s also why we want to make room for stories that look nothing like his.

Sources: E18/E23/E32; W02.

Something useful for your next step.


Personal reflections. Practical questions. Resources worth exploring. We’re bringing them together to help you navigate life without alcohol in a way that makes sense for you.

We’re building what comes next.


Community is the starting point. Our longer-term vision includes places for recovery, more ways to connect with support, and experiences that bring life without alcohol into everyday living.

Stay connected as ZeroBooze grows.


Get new reflections, useful resources, and updates on what’s taking shape. Choose to hear from us. Unsubscribe whenever you want.

sections.title: Website copy — About
sections.body:
HERO
Our story starts with Keith.
It makes room for yours.


ZeroBooze was born in the early days of Keith Polaski’s sobriety, from a need he knew firsthand: a way to connect, find something useful, and build a life without alcohol that belonged to him.


That experience started the brand. The belief behind it reaches further. You own your story. You own your path. Support should respect both.


Sources: E18/E23/E32; W02.


OUR BELIEF
We can walk with you.


The work of change is personal. No brand can do it for you. But connection can matter. So can a perspective you hadn’t considered, a resource you can use, or a conversation you didn’t know how to start.


We’re building ZeroBooze around those possibilities. A community shaped by different experiences, with empathy, personal ownership, and a willingness to keep asking what would help.


Sources: E09/E19/E32.


KEITH’S STORY — first-person draft for Keith’s review
I’ve spent much of my life building businesses. For a long time, alcohol was part of that life too. At work. At celebrations. On hard days. Eventually, more and more of it happened alone.


I kept showing up. I kept building. I told myself that meant I was in control. It became harder to be honest about what alcohol was costing me and the people closest to me.


When I chose to seek help, I was scared. Recovery asked me to look at myself differently. It also gave me a reason to think about what I wanted to build next.


ZeroBooze began there.


I’m still doing the work. I’m sharing my experience because someone else may recognize part of their own. Your life may look very different from mine. Your reasons may be different too.


What I want to build is something useful: a place for connection, resources, and honest conversations about life without alcohol.


I can’t do the work for you. I hope we can walk some of the path together.


Keith Polaski
Founder, ZeroBooze


Sources: adapted from W02 and the origin draft in E18, with E32’s ownership principle. This is proposed founder copy, not a verbatim statement or approved personal disclosure. Confirm personal history and present-day wording with Keith.


WHO THIS IS FOR
For people in recovery.
For people quietly concerned about their drinking.
For people who have lived without alcohol for years.
For people curious about a different way to live.


You don’t need the same history to find a connection.


Button: Explore Resources
Secondary button: Share a Note
Sources: E23/E32.

Title: About ZeroBooze | Our Story and Belief
Description: Learn why Keith Polaski started ZeroBooze and how personal ownership, empathy, and community shape its vision for life without alcohol.

HERO
A place for recovery.
Built around the person.


We’re working toward a ZeroBooze residence where personal ownership, meaningful support, and community can shape the experience of recovery.


The plans are still developing. The residence is not open, and we are not accepting residents through this page.


Sources: E25/E32/E39; W03. Operational status must be reconfirmed before publication.


THE INTENTION
Start with what would help.


A place for recovery should be shaped by the people who come there. Their lives. Their questions. The work they’re ready to do. The support that continues to matter when they leave.


That is the intention guiding this development. As decisions become real, we’ll explain what the residence will offer, who it will serve, and how the experience will work.


Sources: E32/E39; W03. Not a promise of a defined care model.

From intention to a place.


We’ll share meaningful milestones as the work develops: site decisions, design progress, the people shaping the approach, and confirmed information about opening.

sections.title: Website copy — Resources
sections.body:
HERO
Useful perspectives.
Room to find your own.


Life without alcohol comes with questions. We’re building a collection of personal reflections, practical ideas, and selected resources to help you explore yours.


Start where you are. Take what is useful.


Sources: E20/E24/E32.


RESOURCE COLLECTIONS — proposed editorial categories

Questions and perspectives for people beginning to look at their relationship with alcohol.


Living Without Alcohol
Everyday experiences, routines, food, and connection. A life that can be shaped around what matters to you.


Finding Support
Information about different kinds of support, with clear links to the people and organizations providing it.


Stories From the Community
Different experiences, shared with permission and in each person’s own voice.


Along the Path
Notes from Keith and the people helping shape ZeroBooze: what we’re learning, what’s developing, and what we’re still working through.


Sources: E19/E23/E24/E32. No resource collection is represented as populated until reviewed content exists.

Each published resource needs an original source, purpose, intended audience, date checked, availability or geographic limits, author credentials where relevant, and a clear distinction between personal experience and professional guidance. sections.title: Website copy — Horizon
sections.body:
HERO
Our Horizon.
What we’re working toward.


ZeroBooze begins with a belief: you own your story and your path to life without alcohol. Our ambition is to build more ways to support that path.


Some pieces are already taking shape. Others are still ideas we’re working through. We’ll be clear about the difference.


Sources: E20/E32/E39.


PLANNED AREAS
Places for Recovery
A vision for residential settings shaped around personal ownership, support, and the experience of the people who come there.


More Ways to Find Support
Exploring virtual professional support, continued connection, and resources for different stages of alcohol-free living.


Everyday Life
Exploring products, partnerships, beverages, nutrition, and experiences that fit a life without alcohol.


A Charitable Future
A vision for a ZeroBooze charitable foundation. Its structure, purpose, and activities are still to be developed.


Community That Grows With Us
Shared stories, meaningful connections, and opportunities to gather as the community takes shape.


Sources: E20/E32/E39. No implied service availability, charitable registration, tax deductibility, partner commitment, or launch schedule.


INVITATION
Help shape what comes next.


What would have helped you? What would help now? Your perspective can inform what we build.


Button: Share Your Perspective
Secondary button: Follow Our Progress
Sources: E32; proposed copy.

Title: Our Horizon | The Future of ZeroBooze
Description: Explore ZeroBooze’s developing vision for community, recovery residences, support, everyday living, and a charitable future.

Facebook: conversation and community participation.
Instagram: short stories, visual identity, useful prompts, everyday alcohol-free living.
YouTube: founder introduction, thoughtful conversations, and longer stories.
Substack or a site-based publication: regular reflections and progress updates. Choose one primary publishing home before duplicating effort.


The platform list is Keith’s initial preference; no current account status or active audience is assumed. Begin with a sustainable cadence, proposed at one substantive note each week plus adaptations, and adjust to response. Keith says rhythm can follow the community. [E24/E32]

Subject: Welcome to ZeroBooze

Thanks for connecting with ZeroBooze.


People come to life without alcohol for different reasons. Some have been here for years. Some are just beginning. Some are still asking questions.


We’re building a community with room for those differences. We’ll share useful resources, personal reflections, and updates as the larger vision takes shape.


Start wherever feels right: read our story, explore resources, or send a note. You choose how much to share.

sections.title: Sales, partnerships, and recruitment
sections.body:
PARTNER OVERVIEW — proposed
ZeroBooze is building a community around life without alcohol, grounded in personal ownership, useful support, and lived experience. We’re interested in collaborators whose work can add something meaningful for that community.


We’re developing the brand deliberately. The right relationship should fit the audience, add practical value, and be clear about what each partner is offering.


Sources: E22/E32.


PARTNER SELECTION — proposed
Evaluate audience fit, product or service quality, credibility, usefulness, relationship type, and disclosure needs. Keith is exploring both resale and affiliate models. Follower count is one input, not the proposition. [E32]
Possible leads: sober activities/golf introduction in E08; beverage/nutrition relationships and cruise idea in E32; potential storytellers in E03. All are leads, not signed partnerships.


RECRUITMENT INTRO — proposed future-opportunity copy
Help shape what comes next.


ZeroBooze is developing a broader vision for life without alcohol, including future residential recovery and support. We’re interested in people who combine expertise with empathy, value personal ownership, and are willing to question assumptions thoughtfully.


As roles are defined, we’ll share what they involve, the qualifications required, and how to apply.


Sources: E39; W03. No active vacancy or clinical appointment is implied.


PROFESSIONAL / REFERRAL COPY — hold until services exist
Build a separate factual description of eligibility, service scope, provider credentials, location, program format, referral process, exclusions, and continued support. Do not use the lifestyle positioning as a substitute for those facts.


INVESTOR CONTENT — separate workstream
The Oct. 12 exchange records Keith’s intention to provide deck inputs around the first week of November; it does not provide an investment thesis or verified projections. Keep investor requests distinct from consumer copy. [E34]
Inputs required: ownership structure, operating entity, site strategy, development status, capital need, financial model, team, clinical leadership, licensing path, evidence, risks, and milestones.


Narrative seed — proposed:
ZeroBooze’s residential ambition grows from lived experience and a commitment to rethink how support is experienced. The investment case must be built from a defined operating model and evidence, with the community brand providing context rather than standing in for diligence.

CONTENT RECORD — use for each new item
Content ID / working title / audience / channel / objective / source IDs and original dates / original contributor / direct evidence or interpretation / offering status / draft / factual review / Keith approval / publication link / published date / next review date.


RULES FOR ATTRIBUTION
Attribute Keith’s words to Keith, Dustin’s proposals to Dustin, and new copy to this working draft. A forwarded message is not proof of agreement. Use the latest explicit direction when earlier advice conflicts; retain the older position in the decision history.


For new language inspired by a source, write “informed by,” not “Keith said.” For verbatim quotations, preserve wording and identify the original date. Link related assets to the email that supplied them.


APPROVAL PATH — recommended
Editorial draft → source and language check → factual/operational review → Keith review → approved version → publish → record live URL.
Clinical claims need appropriate expert review and evidence before entering approved consumer copy. No automatic scheduling or posting is authorized by this document.


SUCCESS MEASURES — proposed
Meaningful replies and story/resource submissions; opted-in subscribers; repeat visits and resource use; qualified partner inquiries; useful feedback from priority audiences; successful resolution of contact/order questions. Track traffic and sentiment as Keith requested. Do not equate follower volume or merchandise sales with recovery outcomes. [E02/E22/E32]

Residence scope, geography, status, and approved terminology.
Any active professional or virtual service and its provider.
Confirmed program design, duration, post-care, and payment terms.
Verified store inventory, materials, price, shipping, and returns.
Working contact route, ownership, response expectation, and privacy notice.
Approved founder history and personal acknowledgments.

Evidence supporting any proposed outcome or comparison claims.

sections.title: Video clip briefs
sections.body:
CLIP C01 — Simple and true
Source: V01, final paragraph.
Locate: “That's ZeroBooze. Simple and true.”
Selection: include the preceding invitation about living without alcohol crossing someone’s mind or heart, then the closing line.
Target: 15–25 seconds, subject to actual footage.
On-screen hook — proposed: What is ZeroBooze?
Caption — proposed: A community taking shape around life without alcohol. Different stories. A path that’s yours. ZeroBooze. Simple and true.
CTA: Meet ZeroBooze.
Editorial note: preserve “we hope to be” context where needed; do not turn an aspiration into a completed offering.


CLIP C02 — On your terms
Source: V01, third paragraph.
Exact transcript selection: “We're trying to build ZeroBooze so that we can assist others that want to be motivated to live a life without alcohol to do so on their terms, but with knowing that there is someone to walk that path with them.”
Target: 20–30 seconds.
Hook — proposed: Your terms. Your path.
Caption — proposed: You own your story and your path. We’re building ZeroBooze with room for both—and with the hope that you’ll find someone to walk with you.
CTA: Read Our Story.
Editorial note: use accurate subtitles rather than replacing Keith’s spoken syntax with polished draft language.


CLIP C03 — A work in progress
Source: V01, second paragraph.
Exact quote: “This is a new lifestyle brand that is a work in progress. The brand is to support a life without alcohol.”
Target: 10–20 seconds.
Hook — proposed: We’re building this together.
Caption — proposed: ZeroBooze is taking shape. We want to share the work, hear what matters to you, and build something useful for life without alcohol.
CTA: Follow Our Progress.
Editorial note: “40-plus years in the making” is personal context, not the age of the business. If used, ask Keith what the phrase means and keep that distinction clear.


CLIP C04 — No labels
Source: V02, final paragraph.
Exact quote: “We're not going to put labels on anybody. Labels are not fair. Everybody's unique.”
Target: 10–15 seconds.
Hook — proposed: You’re more than a label.
Caption — proposed: People arrive here with different histories and different reasons. You get to decide what your story means.
CTA: Meet the Community.
Editorial note: use a working community destination; otherwise use About.


CLIP C05 — Room for different reasons
Source: V02, middle paragraph.
Locate: “the sober curious” through “they have an important place in the community.”
Target: 20–30 seconds.
Hook — proposed: There’s room for your reason.
Caption — proposed: Some people come to life without alcohol through recovery. Others are curious about how it might fit their lives. The reasons can be different. The invitation can still be shared.
CTA: Explore Resources.
Editorial note: Keith’s “fairly large segment” and “primarily younger adults” are his perspective. Avoid using those descriptions as statistical factoids without independent evidence. A concise selection can focus on the invitation.


CLIP C06 — Content for different stages
Source: V02, first paragraph.
Exact opening: “I think we need to make sure that there's content for the recovered and content for the recovering.”
Target: 15–25 seconds with surrounding context.
Hook — proposed: Different stages. Different needs.
Caption — proposed: What is useful at the beginning may differ from what matters years later. We want ZeroBooze to make room for those differences.
CTA: Tell Us What Would Help.
Editorial note: do not make viewers choose a public label or disclose their recovery stage.


CLIP C07 — You’re not alone
Source: V03, first paragraph.
Exact quote: “For successful lives without alcohol, you need to know that you're not alone on this path.”
Target: 10–20 seconds with context.
Hook — proposed: Someone to walk with you.
Caption — proposed: Connection matters to Keith. It’s one of the reasons he’s building ZeroBooze around community.
CTA: Start a Conversation.
Editorial note: attribute this to Keith’s belief; do not frame it as a guaranteed or proven outcome of joining ZeroBooze.


CLIP C08 — “That’s me”
Source: V03, second paragraph.
Exact quote: “Hopefully the platform encourages people to share their stories so that others can say, ‘Ah, that's me. I've experienced that before.’”
Target: 15–20 seconds.
Hook — proposed: Recognition can start a conversation.
Caption — proposed: Sometimes another person’s story helps you recognize something in your own. Share only what you choose. We’ll ask before publishing it.

sections.title: Values — how we act
sections.body:
PROPOSED BRAND FOUNDATION — October 26, 2026
New strategic language for Keith’s review. Informed by the source hub and confirmed brand rules; not a verbatim founder statement or a claim that future services are operating.

1. RESPECT THE WHOLE PERSON
A person is more than a label, a difficult chapter, or a shared experience with alcohol. Listen before assuming. Respect differences and the decision to keep something personal.
Behavior: ask how someone wants their story used; get permission before sharing it.
Decision test: does this preserve the person’s dignity and choice?

2. PAIR OWNERSHIP WITH SUPPORT
People have agency in their own lives. They also deserve help that meets their needs. Accountability should come with empathy and room for professional care.
Behavior: invite a next step without issuing a verdict or implying someone should do everything alone.
Decision test: are we encouraging agency without adding blame?

3. PUT CONNECTION FIRST
Build relationships around usefulness, participation, and mutual regard. A purchase, public disclosure, or polished story is not the price of belonging.
Behavior: make resources easy to reach; offer ways to participate quietly; keep merchandise secondary.
Decision test: would this still be useful to someone who never buys anything?

4. BE HONEST ABOUT THE WORK
Say what exists, what we know, and what is still developing. Make the strength of a claim match the evidence behind it.
Behavior: distinguish concept visuals from built spaces, founder experience from professional credentials, and future plans from available services.
Decision test: could someone reasonably misunderstand what we are offering today?

5. MAKE IT USEFUL, THEN KEEP IMPROVING
Listen, learn, and turn good intentions into things people can use. Question a convention when there is a clear reason, then show the work behind a better approach.
Behavior: act on feedback, check resources, and explain meaningful changes.
Decision test: what practical value does this add, and how will we know?

HOW TO USE THE VALUES
Values guide team conduct, partner choices, editorial decisions, and the experience of the brand. They are behavioral commitments, not claims that a future residential program has already delivered results.

SOURCE BASIS
E02, E09, E23, E24, E32; V02–V04; confirmed story ownership, community-first direction, and evidence boundaries in hub Sections 4–6.

New strategic language for Keith’s review. Informed by the source hub and confirmed brand rules; not a verbatim founder statement or a claim that future services are operating.

INTERNAL POSITIONING STATEMENT
For people in recovery and people quietly questioning alcohol’s place in their lives, ZeroBooze is a developing brand and community around life without alcohol. Built from lived experience, it brings together useful perspectives and opportunities for connection while working toward a wider vision for recovery and support. It respects the individual’s ownership of their story and makes room for the everyday life they want to build.

THE ROLE
A thoughtful companion and a purposeful builder: help people find something useful now, and be clear about what we are working toward next.

WHAT WE WANT PEOPLE TO UNDERSTAND
This began with someone who needed it first.
There is room for experiences that look different from his.
Your story and your choices remain yours.
Life without alcohol can hold more than the absence of drinking.

CREDIBILITY TO BUILD FROM
Keith’s lived experience and clearly attributed founder perspective.
His stated commitment to helping people find and embrace life without alcohol.
Useful, source-grounded content and transparent development updates as they are delivered.

DISTINCTION TO DEMONSTRATE
Ownership with companionship. A community larger than its founder’s story. Everyday life alongside a wider recovery vision. These are strategic directions to make tangible, not independently proven competitive advantages or exclusive claims.

PUBLIC DESCRIPTION
ZeroBooze is a community taking shape around life without alcohol, with room for different stories, useful perspectives, and a path that belongs to you.

sections.title: Brand pillars — what our messages return to
sections.body:
PROPOSED BRAND FOUNDATION — October 26, 2026
New strategic language for Keith’s review. Informed by the source hub and confirmed brand rules; not a verbatim founder statement or a claim that future services are operating.

PILLAR 1 — YOUR STORY BELONGS TO YOU
Core idea: people can share a connection without sharing the same history or identity.
Message: your experience matters, and you decide what to share.
Expression: “Your story is yours. There’s room for it here.”
Use in: Our Story, founder content, community stories, consent language, invitations to contribute.
Evidence: founder and community transcripts, used in context; actual consent practices.
Creative cue: different people and ordinary details; avoid reducing someone to a symbolic recovery portrait.

PILLAR 2 — YOUR PATH, WITH SUPPORT
Core idea: ownership and companionship belong together.
Message: the work is personal, and appropriate support can be part of it.
Expression: “A next step that’s yours. People to walk with you.”
Use in: Resources, Inquire, future service explanations, thoughtful calls to action.
Evidence: clear resource links, a functioning inquiry route, and verified services only when available.
Creative cue: agency and forward movement; avoid rescue imagery or language suggesting willpower is sufficient.

PILLAR 3 — BELONGING WITHOUT LABELS
Core idea: connection should not require a purchase, a public declaration, or a prescribed identity.
Message: you can start with a question, read quietly, or bring your own perspective.
Expression: “You don’t need the same story to belong.”
Use in: The Community, Find Your People, welcome messages, social prompts.
Evidence: accessible content, optional participation, and respectful handling of submissions.
Creative cue: natural connection and room to participate at different levels; no invented testimonials or community scale.

PILLAR 4 — A LIFE TO LOOK FORWARD TO
Core idea: the ambition includes the life someone wants to make room for beyond alcohol.
Message: everyday enjoyment, relationships, and personal interests deserve space in the story.
Expression: “What do you want to make room for?”
Use in: Living Zero, lifestyle content, editorial themes, and the End game message.
Evidence: thoughtful everyday content and consented individual experiences; do not imply these prove recovery outcomes.
Creative cue: credible ordinary moments; warmth and possibility without glossy perfection.

HOW TO APPLY THE PILLARS
Choose one lead pillar for a module or execution; a supporting pillar can deepen it. Do not force all four into every headline. Values describe how we behave; pillars describe the messages we return to. Mission and vision set their purpose.

EDITORIAL CONTINUITY
This four-pillar system refines the earlier working message pillars in hub Section 4. The earlier Build deliberately and Question conventions themes remain important and are now captured primarily in the values Be honest about the work and Make it useful, then keep improving.

SOURCE BASIS
E09, E23, E24, E32; V01–V04; existing hub Section 4 and Dave’s End game theme. All expression lines are proposed copy, not founder quotations.

sections.title: Personality — how the brand feels
sections.body:
PROPOSED BRAND FOUNDATION — October 26, 2026
New strategic language for Keith’s review. Informed by the source hub and confirmed brand rules; not a verbatim founder statement or a claim that future services are operating.

HUMAN
Speak to a person. Show interest in their experience. Leave room for uncertainty and for more than one way of describing a life.

CANDID
Say something clear and true. Avoid dramatizing a story, minimizing difficulty, or polishing away the parts that make it believable.

ASSURED
Give people a useful starting point. Confidence comes from clarity and care, not volume, superiority, or promises we cannot substantiate.

THOUGHTFUL
Make deliberate choices about language, imagery, access, and consent. Create a premium feeling through attention and respect.

PURPOSEFUL
Build toward something useful. Show progress through concrete decisions and completed work rather than announcing disruption as a personality.

IN ONE SENTENCE
A candid, thoughtful companion with the determination of a builder.

FOR DESIGNERS
Give words and people room. Use clear hierarchy, calm pacing, legible type, and deliberate details. Show lived-in human moments and label concept property imagery. The person should remain more important than a visual metaphor.

INTERPRETATION: our reading of the pattern across sources.
PROPOSED COPY: new language written for review.
FUTURE / UNVERIFIED: a plan or claim that cannot yet be presented as an available service or established result.


Each strategic point and copy module includes source IDs. The source register at the end identifies the email files and links back to them. Dates cited in the discussion are the original conversation dates, rather than simply the October forwarding dates.


Coverage: the message text and forwarded conversations in 39 individual email files; Keith’s September 2026 DOCX attachment; the Anti Talking Points PDF attachment; the current website’s homepage, founder story, notebook, and store preview; and all four supplied video transcripts. Sections 21–23 add transcript-based social content and Keith’s bio. Design files, photographs, legal agreements, and other embedded attachments have not all been visually reviewed. Transcript wording is source material; actual recordings, clip timecodes, and picture edits still require verification.


Later additions should record source, owner, date, audience, channel, availability status, copy status, and approval. Preserve earlier decisions in the decision log when direction changes.

items.title: What Keith is trying to build
items.body:
CONFIRMED DIRECTION
ZeroBooze is bigger than merchandise. Keith wants empathy and support, acknowledgment of the individual in each story, and navigation toward life without alcohol. He describes the ambition as the “Waze” of sobriety. Community and in-residence development should move in parallel, on different timelines. [E32 attachment, Sept. 12]


His priority audiences are the Recovering and the Quietly Concerned. People own their story and their path. Accountability matters, but the tone should carry it subtly and deliberately. His central distinction: ZB cannot do the work FOR someone, but can do it WITH them. [E32]


He wants community participation, shared stories, eventual gatherings, useful resources, and invitations to help shape the brand. Merchandise remains available for those who want it; it is ancillary. [E09, July 7; E32]


He wants the brand to feel premium, conversational, and clear without being in someone’s face. Softness does not come naturally to him; he explicitly asks for help balancing his directness. He wants the founder story early, while preserving the feeling that this is about the visitor. [E32]


INTERPRETATION
Keith is a builder who wants lived experience to lead to useful change. His frustration with familiar recovery conventions fuels ambition, but his strongest public message is practical companionship and personal ownership. “Disruption” should be demonstrated by concrete choices and evidence as they develop.


The brand needs two speeds: a clear, useful community experience people can enter now, and a longer-term vision with transparent milestones. A visitor should not have to decipher which is which. [E20, E25, E29–E30, E32; W01–W03]


WORKING POSITIONING — proposed
ZeroBooze is a community taking shape around life without alcohol, built from lived experience and grounded in the belief that you own your story and your path. It brings people, perspectives, and useful resources together, while working toward a broader future in recovery and support. [E09, E23, E32]


SHORT DESCRIPTION — proposed
Life without alcohol. Your story. Your path. A community to walk with you.


Use that as descriptive copy, not an assumed approved tagline. Keith agreed that the name can stand alone. [E25, Aug. 28]

items.title: Audience priorities
items.body:
The Recovering — primary
Keith defines this audience as day one through five years in his internal notes. Their need: continued support, useful next steps, and a connection beyond a single episode of care. Message: you are doing the work; you do not have to navigate every part alone. Avoid making the five-year boundary a public clinical definition. [E32]


The Quietly Concerned — primary
People at the doorstep of change who have not taken that step. Their need: recognition, privacy, and a manageable invitation. Message: you can start with a question. Do not assume they identify with recovery or publicly disclose concerns. [E25, E23, E32]


The Recovered — secondary
Keith’s internal definition is five-plus years. Their need: identity, connection, contribution, and respect for experience. Message: your perspective can help someone find their next step. Avoid suggesting they have crossed a universal finish line. [E32]


The Sober Curious — secondary
People considering alcohol-free living, including for health or lifestyle reasons, without assuming an abuse history. Message: there is room for your reason. [E23, E32]


Additional communication audiences — proposed
Loved ones seeking a way to support someone; professionals and referral partners assessing credibility; potential employees and collaborators; partners and donors; investors considering the future residential vision. These require different proof and calls to action. Do not make investor ambition the homepage’s primary message.


Decision history
Dustin’s July 7 recommendation emphasized people already living without alcohol and deferred sober curious outreach. Keith’s September notes broadened the model and explicitly prioritized the Recovering and Quietly Concerned. The September notes guide this draft. [E09 → E25/E23 → E32]

items.title: Source foundation — earlier voice & message pillars
items.body:
SOURCE AND DECISION HISTORY
This earlier working interpretation is preserved for reference. The proposed October 26 Brand pillars and Voice & tone modules provide the current organized system for review. No client approval is implied.

VOICE — proposed application of Keith’s direction
Conversational, direct, warm, and sure of itself. Use short clear sentences alongside natural paragraphs. Address a person rather than a demographic category. Make room for uncertainty without sounding vague. Offer participation without demanding disclosure. Use empathy with accountability; do not moralize or promise to save anyone. [E10, E18–E19, E23–E25, E32; W02]


PILLAR A: Your story belongs to you
You own your story and your path. Different histories can share a common connection without being flattened into the founder’s experience. [E23, E32; W03]
Use in: homepage, About, invitations to share, community guidelines.


PILLAR B: We can walk with you
Support and useful navigation accompany personal effort. Make the next step feel approachable and specific. [E32]
Use in: Resources, Contact, support descriptions, after-care communications when a service exists.


PILLAR C: Belonging comes first
Community is a priority, not a by-product of shopping. Merchandise expresses connection; purchasing is not a condition of participation. [E09, E22, E32]
Use in: homepage order, Store, email welcome, social.


PILLAR D: Build deliberately; show the work
The brand is in development. Updates, questions, and milestones can make progress visible and invite collaboration. [E24, E32; W03]
Use in: Horizon, notebook, recruitment, investor materials.


PILLAR E: Question conventions with care
Challenge assumptions about the experience of recovery, with specific reasons and substantiation. Lead with what improves life for the individual. [E02, E25, E29]
Use in: thought leadership and program development; avoid unsupported comparisons in public sales copy.


Recognition, permission, and relief are a useful editorial test proposed by Dustin, not a documented final emotional choice by Keith. Pair that test with Keith’s explicit “empathy and support.” [E19 vs. E32]


BEFORE / AFTER — editorial examples
Generic: “Embark on an inspiring journey.”
Proposed: “Find a next step that makes sense for you.”
Generic: “We will transform your life.”
Proposed: “You own the work. We want to help you find the people and resources to support it.”
Generic: “Our facility treats patients.”
Proposed future description: “Our planned residence will be shaped around the people who come here for recovery.”

items.title: Keith’s language guide
items.body:
Source: E39, ZB Anti Talking Points PDF. These are Keith’s preferred contrasts, recorded faithfully. They are an internal direction list, not evidence that planned clinical offerings or outcomes exist.


Avoid → Keith’s preferred wording
Treatment → Relief / Recovery
Journey → Path
One Day at a Time → Your own Horizon
“AA” Foundation → Ownership Foundation
Traditional / Accepted Treatment → Disruption Treatment
Patients → Resident Guests
Alcoholism → Abuse
Inspire → Self-Realization
30 Days & 60 Days → 45 Days & 75 Days
Acceptance → Admission
12% Outcome → 35% Outcome (3X)
Self-Serve Post Care → Administered Post Care
Static / Accepted Modalities → Disruption Modalities
Groups → Community
Insurance Pay → High Self-Pay
Profit Focused → Success Focused
Varying Residential Rules → Regimented Residential Rules


Additional explicit preferences
Facility: avoid in public brand language; Dave’s current brief confirms this preference. Proposed replacement: “Our Residence,” subject to confirming there is a single residential property. “Our Spaces” works if the page covers several locations or nonresidential settings.
Quietly Committed: superseded by Quietly Concerned. [E25, E23, E32]
“Live inside”: Keith questioned it; use experience, commonality, expression, or support instead. [E23]
Road: Keith explicitly asks to replace it with path. [E32]
“Inspire / Journey / Celebrate” as a logo lockup: challenged by Dustin, followed by Keith’s pivot toward the name alone. [E15, E25]
“Celebrating Sobriety, Inspiring Recovery”: considered, then set aside; not the default tagline. [E21, E25]


HOW TO APPLY
Prefer recovery, relief, support, path, ownership, community, and life without alcohol. “Resident Guests” belongs in an actual residential context; use person, community member, or participant elsewhere. Avoid defining someone as “an abuser.” Even though “Abuse” appears on Keith’s list, person-centered plain language often removes the need for a label.


The list is not a mechanical word-replacement tool. “Admission” can mean entering a program; do not replace emotional acceptance everywhere. “Disruption Treatment” still uses a word Keith otherwise dislikes, so retain that exact contrast in the internal register while writing public copy around the specific approach.


Do not convert 45/75-day plans, self-pay positioning, administered post care, residential rules, or numerical outcomes into current service facts. All require operational confirmation. The 12% / 35% / 3X line is an unverified claim and is excluded from public copy.


Respect different approaches to recovery. Ownership is the brand’s organizing idea; it does not establish that the brand rejects all spiritual or peer-support options. The PDF’s appendix describes several alternatives with differing philosophies, including 12-step approaches. Do not copy that appendix as verified current resource guidance without checking the original providers.

LATEST LANGUAGE UPDATE — October 14, 2026
Dave’s direction: Patients is wording to avoid; Resident Guests is the preferred wording. This supersedes the earlier Patient → Resident entry. Use the residential term in the appropriate context.

BRAND NAME — confirmed October 14, 2026
Always write ZeroBooze as one word, with a capital Z and B. See the Brand name & spelling module.

items.title: Decisions, tensions, and evidence boundaries
items.body:
DECISIONS TO CARRY FORWARD
Community is a priority. [Keith, E09, July 7]
Let ZeroBooze stand on its own; the tagline discussion has changed. [Keith, E25, Aug. 28; E21 forwarding note]
Use Quietly Concerned and prioritize that audience alongside the Recovering. [Keith, E23/E32, Sept. 4/12]
Keep merchandise secondary. [Keith, E32]
Use conversational copy with deliberate accountability. [Keith, E32]
Develop community and residential ambitions in parallel on different timelines. [Keith, E32]
Use opt-in updates and communications. [Keith, E32]
Allow both Gratitude and Interview in Progress to coexist as personal practices. [Keith, E13, Sept. 19]
Preserve a Horizon space for future ambitions. [Keith, E20, Sept. 7]


TENSIONS TO RESOLVE THROUGH DESIGN AND COPY
Quiet public voice versus “let’s break things” internal energy: keep the public welcome calm; demonstrate challenge through substantive content. [E25/E32]
Founder authenticity versus a community larger than one person: use Keith’s story to open the door, then turn toward the visitor and other voices. [E22/E32]
Lifestyle brand versus residential provider: one brand can connect them, but available services and future plans must be unmistakable. Dustin suggested separate sites; Keith later emphasized parallel efforts. Architecture remains a decision, not a settled mandate. [E30/E32]
Privacy versus direct access: Keith wants a brand-facing conversation channel, not his personal number prominently displayed. Verify workflow and response expectations before activating it. [E32; W01]
Premium versus accessible: dignity and clarity should create the premium feeling without implying everyone must shop or afford residential care.


CLAIMS HELD FROM PUBLIC COPY
Claims about the historical origin of 28-day programs: present in E25/E29, not independently substantiated here.
Numerical recovery outcomes and “3X”: present in E39, no definition, denominator, follow-up period, or supporting evidence supplied.
Market-size, alcohol-cancer awareness, competitor revenue, and closure assertions in E17: research leads, not approved proof points.
Specific advocate identities and willingness to participate: E03 is too ambiguous to establish an endorsement.
Clinical modalities, staffing, licenses, accreditations, program eligibility, pricing, insurance terms, residence location, opening date, and availability: not confirmed for launch.
Shock Pulse Medical: separate venture in E07/E35/E36. Do not imply its technology or services are part of ZeroBooze without an explicit decision and evidence.

items.title: Current website review
items.body:
Reviewed October 13, 2026 at https://zerobooze.life/ through the visible site.


W01 — Homepage
Current lead: “You remember the moment.” Describes a brand taking shape around life without alcohol. Includes founder story, community, notebook, hat, and conversation invitation. Retain the human welcome and room for different experiences; make the purpose clearer sooner. The opening assumes a defining moment, which may fit less well for sober curious visitors.


W02 — Founder story, https://zerobooze.life/story
Current title: “I’m still in it.” The story acknowledges alcohol’s effects, prior attempts at change, choosing care, and building ZeroBooze while still in recovery. Keep its candor. Replace dated early-recovery timing and confirm personal details before republication. The personal thank-you names family and supporters; retain only with Keith’s approval of placement and wording. Use “recovery” rather than “treatment” in new brand copy while preserving exact quoted source records.


W03 — Keith’s Notebook, opened from homepage
Topics: common denominator across different histories; development of a first center in Florida; and the need for clinical, design, and construction expertise. It expressly states the center is not open. Preserve that availability distinction. These entries corroborate a development effort, not an operational residence.


Current site limitation
Texting is explicitly a preview and is not connected. Do not publish “Text ZeroBooze” as a working action until verified. Navigation and page structure differ from the requested new sitemap.


This review is a baseline, not a commitment to reuse the current design or all copy. The website draft below rebuilds the message around the primary audiences and Keith’s later direction.


W04 — Store, https://zerobooze.life/merch
The visible collection preview lists hat, cap, visor, tumbler, polo, jug, and clear tumbler. It expressly says products, prices, and options are proposed for review and purchases are not enabled. The repeated $35 display is not adopted as approved pricing. Confirm the catalog, stock, fulfillment, and checkout before publishing Store copy.

items.title: Recommended website architecture
items.body:
Recommended main navigation:
About | Our Residence | Services | Resources | Store | Contact
Home is reached through the logo. Add Horizon as a visible secondary link and a prominent homepage module.


Home: explain what ZeroBooze means, invite the priority audiences, introduce community and Keith, and offer a useful next step.
About / Our Story: the belief, founder origin, audience, and approach. Prefer a personal story to a conventional resume bio. [E18, E29–E30, E32]
Our Residence: proposed replacement for Facility. While development continues, this page describes the intention and progress; it must not resemble an admissions page.
Services: show available ways to engage first; label any clinical or residential offerings in development. If no services are operational, consider “Support” for the public navigation, with “Services” retained as the working sitemap label.
Resources: practical guidance, selected links, shared experiences, and the ongoing notebook. Proposed notebook label: “Along the Path.” Keith asked to reconsider “Notebook”; this label is a recommendation, not his approved wording. [E32]
Store: merchandise and expression, with truthful product information and clear fulfillment policies.
Contact: a modest, usable invitation for general inquiries, stories, partners, and recruitment.
Horizon: future centers, resources, virtual support, beverages/nutrition, and a charitable foundation, without implying launch dates. [E20, E39]


Primary conversion recommendation: a conversation or optional updates, supported by useful Resources. Buying is secondary. Keith’s stated goal is helping people live without alcohol and tell others, with traffic and positive feedback as early signals. [E32]

items.title: Website copy — About
items.body:
HERO
Our story starts with Keith.
It makes room for yours.


ZeroBooze was born in the early days of Keith Polaski’s sobriety, from a need he knew firsthand: a way to connect, find something useful, and build a life without alcohol that belonged to him.


That experience started the brand. The belief behind it reaches further. You own your story. You own your path. Support should respect both.


Sources: E18/E23/E32; W02.


OUR BELIEF
We can walk with you.


The work of change is personal. No brand can do it for you. But connection can matter. So can a perspective you hadn’t considered, a resource you can use, or a conversation you didn’t know how to start.


We’re building ZeroBooze around those possibilities. A community shaped by different experiences, with empathy, personal ownership, and a willingness to keep asking what would help.


Sources: E09/E19/E32.


KEITH’S STORY — first-person draft for Keith’s review
I’ve spent much of my life building businesses. For a long time, alcohol was part of that life too. At work. At celebrations. On hard days. Eventually, more and more of it happened alone.


I kept showing up. I kept building. I told myself that meant I was in control. It became harder to be honest about what alcohol was costing me and the people closest to me.


When I chose to seek help, I was scared. Recovery asked me to look at myself differently. It also gave me a reason to think about what I wanted to build next.


ZeroBooze began there.


I’m still doing the work. I’m sharing my experience because someone else may recognize part of their own. Your life may look very different from mine. Your reasons may be different too.


What I want to build is something useful: a place for connection, resources, and honest conversations about life without alcohol.


I can’t do the work for you. I hope we can walk some of the path together.


Keith Polaski
Founder, ZeroBooze


Sources: adapted from W02 and the origin draft in E18, with E32’s ownership principle. This is proposed founder copy, not a verbatim statement or approved personal disclosure. Confirm personal history and present-day wording with Keith.


WHO THIS IS FOR
For people in recovery.
For people quietly concerned about their drinking.
For people who have lived without alcohol for years.
For people curious about a different way to live.


You don’t need the same history to find a connection.


Button: Explore Resources
Secondary button: Share a Note
Sources: E23/E32.

items.body:
HERO
Our Horizon.
What we’re working toward.


ZeroBooze begins with a belief: you own your story and your path to life without alcohol. Our ambition is to build more ways to support that path.


Some pieces are already taking shape. Others are still ideas we’re working through. We’ll be clear about the difference.


Sources: E20/E32/E39.


PLANNED AREAS
Places for Recovery
A vision for residential settings shaped around personal ownership, support, and the experience of the people who come there.


More Ways to Find Support
Exploring virtual professional support, continued connection, and resources for different stages of alcohol-free living.


Everyday Life
Exploring products, partnerships, beverages, nutrition, and experiences that fit a life without alcohol.


A Charitable Future
A vision for a ZeroBooze charitable foundation. Its structure, purpose, and activities are still to be developed.


Community That Grows With Us
Shared stories, meaningful connections, and opportunities to gather as the community takes shape.


Sources: E20/E32/E39. No implied service availability, charitable registration, tax deductibility, partner commitment, or launch schedule.


INVITATION
Help shape what comes next.


What would have helped you? What would help now? Your perspective can inform what we build.


Button: Share Your Perspective
Secondary button: Follow Our Progress
Sources: E32; proposed copy.

items.title: Sales, partnerships, and recruitment
items.body:
PARTNER OVERVIEW — proposed
ZeroBooze is building a community around life without alcohol, grounded in personal ownership, useful support, and lived experience. We’re interested in collaborators whose work can add something meaningful for that community.


We’re developing the brand deliberately. The right relationship should fit the audience, add practical value, and be clear about what each partner is offering.


Sources: E22/E32.


PARTNER SELECTION — proposed
Evaluate audience fit, product or service quality, credibility, usefulness, relationship type, and disclosure needs. Keith is exploring both resale and affiliate models. Follower count is one input, not the proposition. [E32]
Possible leads: sober activities/golf introduction in E08; beverage/nutrition relationships and cruise idea in E32; potential storytellers in E03. All are leads, not signed partnerships.


RECRUITMENT INTRO — proposed future-opportunity copy
Help shape what comes next.


ZeroBooze is developing a broader vision for life without alcohol, including future residential recovery and support. We’re interested in people who combine expertise with empathy, value personal ownership, and are willing to question assumptions thoughtfully.


As roles are defined, we’ll share what they involve, the qualifications required, and how to apply.


Sources: E39; W03. No active vacancy or clinical appointment is implied.


PROFESSIONAL / REFERRAL COPY — hold until services exist
Build a separate factual description of eligibility, service scope, provider credentials, location, program format, referral process, exclusions, and continued support. Do not use the lifestyle positioning as a substitute for those facts.


INVESTOR CONTENT — separate workstream
The Oct. 12 exchange records Keith’s intention to provide deck inputs around the first week of November; it does not provide an investment thesis or verified projections. Keep investor requests distinct from consumer copy. [E34]
Inputs required: ownership structure, operating entity, site strategy, development status, capital need, financial model, team, clinical leadership, licensing path, evidence, risks, and milestones.


Narrative seed — proposed:
ZeroBooze’s residential ambition grows from lived experience and a commitment to rethink how support is experienced. The investment case must be built from a defined operating model and evidence, with the community brand providing context rather than standing in for diligence.

items.title: Content operations and approval record
items.body:
CONTENT RECORD — use for each new item
Content ID / working title / audience / channel / objective / source IDs and original dates / original contributor / direct evidence or interpretation / offering status / draft / factual review / Keith approval / publication link / published date / next review date.


RULES FOR ATTRIBUTION
Attribute Keith’s words to Keith, Dustin’s proposals to Dustin, and new copy to this working draft. A forwarded message is not proof of agreement. Use the latest explicit direction when earlier advice conflicts; retain the older position in the decision history.


For new language inspired by a source, write “informed by,” not “Keith said.” For verbatim quotations, preserve wording and identify the original date. Link related assets to the email that supplied them.


APPROVAL PATH — recommended
Editorial draft → source and language check → factual/operational review → Keith review → approved version → publish → record live URL.
Clinical claims need appropriate expert review and evidence before entering approved consumer copy. No automatic scheduling or posting is authorized by this document.


SUCCESS MEASURES — proposed
Meaningful replies and story/resource submissions; opted-in subscribers; repeat visits and resource use; qualified partner inquiries; useful feedback from priority audiences; successful resolution of contact/order questions. Track traffic and sentiment as Keith requested. Do not equate follower volume or merchandise sales with recovery outcomes. [E02/E22/E32]


NEXT INPUTS THAT CHANGE THE COPY
Operational status: what actually exists today?
Residence scope, geography, status, and approved terminology.
Any active professional or virtual service and its provider.
Confirmed program design, duration, post-care, and payment terms.
Verified store inventory, materials, price, shipping, and returns.
Working contact route, ownership, response expectation, and privacy notice.
Approved founder history and personal acknowledgments.
Verify clip timecodes and transcript wording against all four master recordings; supplied transcripts are now incorporated in Sections 21–23.
Approval of “Our Residence,” “Along the Path,” public audience language, and Horizon placement.
Evidence supporting any proposed outcome or comparison claims.

CONTENT TYPES

Quote cards: exact excerpts, attributed to Keith and the source.

Factoids: verified brand facts or carefully sourced external information.

CLIP C01 — Simple and true

Source: V01, final paragraph.

Selection: include the preceding invitation about living without alcohol crossing someone’s mind or heart, then the closing line.
Target: 15–25 seconds, subject to actual footage.

Caption — proposed: A community taking shape around life without alcohol. Different stories. A path that’s yours. ZeroBooze. Simple and true.
CTA: Meet ZeroBooze.
Editorial note: preserve “we hope to be” context where needed; do not turn an aspiration into a completed offering.

items.title: On your terms
items.body:
CLIP C02 — On your terms

Source: V01, third paragraph.
Exact transcript selection: “We're trying to build ZeroBooze so that we can assist others that want to be motivated to live a life without alcohol to do so on their terms, but with knowing that there is someone to walk that path with them.”
Target: 20–30 seconds.
Hook — proposed: Your terms. Your path.
Caption — proposed: You own your story and your path. We’re building ZeroBooze with room for both—and with the hope that you’ll find someone to walk with you.
CTA: Read Our Story.
Editorial note: use accurate subtitles rather than replacing Keith’s spoken syntax with polished draft language.

items.title: Extended bio
items.body:
Keith Polaski founded ZeroBooze in the early days of his own sobriety. After years spent building businesses, he began working on something more personal: a brand and community shaped around life without alcohol.


ZeroBooze grows from a belief that people own their story and their path. Keith wants it to offer connection, useful perspectives, and room for experiences that differ from his own. He is particularly focused on people in recovery and people who are privately beginning to question the role alcohol plays in their lives.


Keith co-founded radius financial group in 1999. Its advisory-board site also identifies his military background.


At ZeroBooze, he hopes to apply his experience as a builder to a broader vision that includes community, future recovery and relief centers, and other ways to support alcohol-free living. Those plans are still developing. His intention is to help people find and embrace life without alcohol on their own terms.
Sources: E23/E32/V01/V02/V04; professional facts P01.
